---
title: Indented cell fence fixture
---

Prose before the cell. The fence below is indented 4 spaces, which CommonMark
calls indented code — but quarto's cell opener is `^\s*` and it validates this
cell, and knitr executes it (both measured firsthand vs 1.7.33, Session 178).

    ```{r}
#| echo: maybe
1
    ```

An indented PLAIN fence is not a fence to quarto either — its plain opener is
column-0 — so it must not open a region that swallows the real cell below it.

    ```
    text
    ```

```{r}
#| echo: maybe
2
```

An UNTERMINATED indented fence builds no cell at all: quarto flushes an unclosed
fence's lines as markdown, so the document renders exit 0 and nothing below is
validated. Flagging here would be a false positive on a document quarto accepts.

    ```{r}
#| echo: maybe
3
